cards.explanation: The answer is the lame, the blind and the mute. The crowds come bringing "…the lame, the blind, the crippled, the mute, and many others…" and they lay them at His feet. And Jesus heals them. They're set right down at His feet, friends, and that's where the healing happens.

The answer is True. The crowd is amazed when they see "…the mute speaking, the crippled restored, the lame walking, and the blind seeing." Then they glorify the God of Israel. That's a whole mountain of people with their jaws on the ground, and then their praise going up.

The answer is eat. Jesus says, "…they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat." He sees what the crowd needs, and He says it out loud to His disciples. Right after that He says, "I have compassion for this crowd…"

The answer is True. Jesus says, "I do not want to send them away hungry, or they may faint along the way." He says it right after telling His disciples, "I have compassion for this crowd…" He's already thinking about what could happen to them along the way.

The answer is that the disciples ask where they could find enough bread out there. They say, "Where in this desolate place could we find enough bread to feed such a large crowd?" They're looking at the empty land and the huge crowd, friends. I'd have asked the same thing, and probably louder.

The answer is sit down. Matthew says, "And He instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground." Jesus gives that instruction to the crowd before the loaves and fish are even taken. Sitting down it is, bakers.

The answer is that He gives thanks. The text says, "Taking the seven loaves and the fish, He gave thanks and broke them." Seven loaves and a few small fish, and Jesus gives thanks. Thanks comes first, friends, and then the breaking.
The answer is False. Matthew says, "They all ate and were satisfied…" That's all of them, not just some. Jesus said He didn't want to send them away hungry, and nobody went away hungry.

The answer is basketfuls of broken pieces. Matthew says, "…the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over." They all ate and were satisfied, and there were still leftovers to pick up. Any baker would love that kind of leftovers.

The answer is that He gets into the boat. Matthew says, "After Jesus had dismissed the crowds, He got into the boat and went to the region of Magadan." He came along the Sea of Galilee, friends, so a boat fits right in.
